scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: Hi, I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod).
I suddenly can't reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) from my machine -- they all just time out for me. My own department's
machines are fine. I have no idea how the departments are joined together,
sorry. Could someone take a look and sort it out? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported fault — that it_hod (192.168.1.2) cannot reach any CS department
machine on 192.168.2.x — is not supported by any evidence found in the live lab.
A comprehensive end-to-end investigation was conducted covering every component
in the described path.

Both it_hod and all five CS machines (cs_hod through cs_lab4, addresses
192.168.2.2–192.168.2.6) have correctly configured IP addresses and default
gateways. Router0, which directly connects the IT LAN (eth0, 192.168.1.1/24)
and the CS LAN (eth1, 192.168.2.1/24), has both interfaces UP, IP forwarding
enabled, and both subnets installed as directly connected routes in its FIB —
no RIP involvement is needed for this inter-LAN path. IPtables on router0 and
on all CS hosts show empty rule chains (policy ACCEPT). Switch0 and switch1
are bridging in forwarding state on all ports. All three routers' FRR daemon
suites (watchfrr, zebra, ripd, mgmtd, staticd) are running normally with
correct RIP configurations and complete routing tables. Bidirectional ICMP
from it_hod to every CS machine and back returns 0% packet loss at 1–2 ms
latency.

The network is operating correctly. The premise of the helpdesk ticket — that
the 192.168.2.x segment is unreachable from it_hod — is false. No fault exists
in the current lab state. The corrective action is simply to inform the user
that connectivity is confirmed healthy and to ask them to re-test from their
machine; if they still observe an issue it is likely transient or local to
their client application rather than a network-layer fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router0's IT and CS interfaces are up and inter-department routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly notes router0's IT and CS interfaces are UP and confirms inter-department routing works (directly connected routes, IP forwarding enabled, 0% ICMP loss).

The agent's log contains direct, repeated successful pings/traceroutes between it_hod and multiple 192.168.2.x hosts, ARP entries, interface states, running routing daemons, and empty firewall rules — all consistent with no network fault. The writeup's conclusions follow from those observed facts, with only minor implicit claims (e.g., explicit ip_forward sysctl output) but well-supported by end-to-end tests.
